docRequirement: changelog.md line 21 (release 2.1.219): "Added `mcp_server_errors` to the headless stream-json init event, listing `--mcp-config` entries skipped by config validation; terminal runs print a startup warning". Two bindings: (a) the headless `--output-format stream-json` stream opens with an init event, and that event carries an `mcp_server_errors` key naming MCP entries the loader skipped during config validation (omitted when there are none, per headless.md, so a CI gate can fail on a non-empty array); (b) the same skip is surfaced as a startup warning on a terminal (non-headless) run.
current: Neither half exists. (1) No init frame at all: `sendAndStream` sets `const streamJson = args.outputFormat === 'stream-json'` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:457) and, inside the `client.on('session:event', ...)` subscription, the only stream-json write is `process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(ev) + '\n')` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:469-471) — a verbatim passthrough of the server's `session:event` payload. Nothing is written to stdout before the first server event on either caller path (`cmdSend` apps/cli/src/index.ts:591, `cmdRun` apps/cli/src/index.ts:852; the run path's pre-turn output is stderr only — apps/cli/src/index.ts:606, :608, :623, :759, :838). (2) No transport for such a frame: the `AgentEvent` union (packages/core/src/types/message.ts:966-1014) and the wire DTO `SessionEvent` union (packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:342-...) have no `init`/`system` member of any spelling. (3) `grep -ran -e 'mcp_server_errors' -e 'mcpServerErrors' packages apps` → 0 hits (run with `-a` for the NUL-byte trap). (4) No `--mcp-config` flag exists: the complete flag list is apps/cli/src/index.ts:80-157 (`--url --token --workspace --timeout --json --tls-ca --send-timeout --source --mode --output-format --json-schema --no-cleanup --disable-spinner/--no-spinner --verbose --safe-mode --server-entry --workspace-dir --provider --model --api-key --base-url --help --version --validate-server`); MCP servers arrive from Sources (`--source <slug>`) and from installed plugins. (5) The data the field would carry is produced and then thrown away: `SourceServerBuilder.buildAll` returns `{ mcpServers, apiServers, errors }` (packages/shared/src/sources/server-builder.ts:323-374), and its single caller drops `errors` — `materializeSourceServers` awaits `buildAll` at packages/shared/src/mcp/runtime-pool-servers.ts:392 and returns `{ sources, mcpServers, apiServers }` at :428, with `built.errors` referenced nowhere; a source whose MCP server failed to build is skipped silently at :414 (`if (!server) continue`). Worse, the genuine config-validation skips never even reach `errors`: a stdio source with no `command` (server-builder.ts:109-112), an HTTP/SSE source with no `url` (:126-129) and an authenticated source with no token (:162-166) each `debug()` and `return null`, and `buildAll` only pushes an entry for the HTTP-auth case (:344-352) or a thrown exception (:365-369). (6) Terminal warning: the CLI's only startup stderr lines are 'Starting server...', the safe-mode notice, 'Server ready:', 'LLM connection configured:' and 'Project selected:' (apps/cli/src/index.ts:606, :608, :623, :759, :838) — nothing MCP-related. (7) The nearest existing surfaces are different events at a different time: plugin-supplied MCP validation diagnostics are reachable headlessly only through the separate `plugin` command (apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:179-186, :252 'MCP servers' group, :314, :447-450), and the only MCP failures the run stream can carry are mid-turn runtime `typed_error`s `mcp_auth_required`/`mcp_unreachable` (packages/core/src/types/message.ts:679-680, raised at packages/shared/src/agent/diagnostics.ts:363, :374).
divergence: Not a key-name difference and not a narrower value: the whole init frame is absent, so there is no object on which to spell `mcp_server_errors`. On top of that the payload has no producer wired to it — MCP config-validation skips are `debug()`-only (server-builder.ts:110, :127, :164), the one aggregated error list that does exist (`BuiltServers.errors`) is discarded by its only consumer (runtime-pool-servers.ts:392 → :428), and the errors are known only when a turn's capability snapshot is materialized, i.e. AFTER the point where an init frame would be emitted. Scope narrowing that survives from the challenge: the field's documented input (`--mcp-config` entries) does not exist in this fork at all, so the implementable requirement is "the init frame reports MCP entries this run skipped", sourced from Sources and plugin MCP configs rather than from a per-invocation config flag. Deduplication: f133, f180 and f125 are one defect — the missing headless init frame — counted three times; f133 is its `mcp_server_errors` field, f125 its framing, f180 its full field set.

change.what: Make a config-validation skip reportable instead of debug-only. Give `buildMcpServer` a way to report why it returned null (either an out-param collector or a discriminated `{ config } | { skipped: { code } }` return) with codes for the three current silent paths: stdio source missing `command` (:109-112), HTTP/SSE source missing `url` (:126-129), authenticated source with no token (:162-166). In `buildAll` (:323-374) push each into the existing `errors: BuiltServers['errors']` list alongside the AUTH_REQUIRED case (:344-352), extending the entry shape from `{ sourceSlug, error }` to also carry a stable `code` so a CI consumer can match on it rather than on prose. Add the codes next to `SERVER_BUILD_ERRORS`.

Stop discarding `built.errors`. It is fetched at :392 and never read; add it (plus an entry for the wire-name skip at :414, `if (!server) continue`) to the returned object at :428 and thread it through the capability-snapshot materialization so the session runtime holds the current run's MCP skip list. This is the producer the init frame needs.

change.symbol: SESSIONS channel map (see the CREATE entry at :25)
change.what: Add one read-only channel, e.g. `sessions:mcpStartupReport`, returning `{ mcpServers: string[]; mcpServerErrors?: { name: string; code: string; message: string }[] }` for a session. Read-only RPC, no new persisted state. Timing note the implementer must resolve: MCP servers are materialized per turn, so either (a) the CLI holds the init line until the runtime has materialized the first snapshot and emits it as the first stdout line once available, or (b) `sessions:create` eagerly materializes the source/plugin MCP set for validation. Pick (a) — it does not change turn semantics.
Register the new channel's handler, reading the skip list threaded out of `materializeSourceServers` for the session's runtime. No change to `sessions:create`'s result shape.

Emit the init frame. When `streamJson`, before the first passthrough write, `process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(init) + '\n')` with `{ type: 'system', subtype: 'init', session_id, model, cwd, mcp_servers, ...(errors.length ? { mcp_server_errors: errors } : {}) }` — the key OMITTED when the list is empty, which is what makes a `jq` CI gate on a non-empty array work. Source the payload from the new RPC. Independently of stream-json, when the list is non-empty write a one-line startup warning to stderr via the existing `err`/`process.stderr.write` path (:246, :606-623) so a terminal run also surfaces it. This is the only user-visible half; it is ~15 lines.

Two cases: with a skipped MCP source, the FIRST stdout line parses as the init frame and its `mcp_server_errors` names the source; with no skips, the init frame is still first and has no `mcp_server_errors` key at all (assert `'mcp_server_errors' in frame === false`, not a falsy check).
Document the stream-json init frame and the `mcp_server_errors` key with its omit-when-empty rule; today the section documents only `text`/`json`/`stream-json` as names.

blastRadius: Crosses a wire boundary — say so explicitly, it is a risk trigger here. (1) The new first stdout line changes the stream-json contract: every consumer of `nessy-general-agent run|send --output-format stream-json` must tolerate a leading non-`session:event` object. Existing consumers in-repo are the tests at apps/cli/src/run.test.ts:213, :338, :372 and the docs at docs/cli.md:165. (2) If the frame is instead added as a new `SessionEvent`/`AgentEvent` member (the alternative to CLI-side synthesis), it touches packages/core/src/types/message.ts:966-1014 and packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:342-... — both are read by the Electron renderer's event reducers as well as the CLI, so every exhaustive switch over the union becomes a compile site. Prefer CLI-side synthesis to keep the union untouched. (3) `BuiltServers['errors']` shape change hits packages/shared/src/sources/server-builder.ts (the JSDoc example at :86 destructures `errors`) and its single caller packages/shared/src/mcp/runtime-pool-servers.ts:392; covered by packages/shared/src/sources/__tests__/. (4) `buildMcpServer`'s signature/return change has exactly one production caller (server-builder.ts:339) — verified by `grep -ran 'buildMcpServer\b'`, 3 hits total, one being a JSDoc line. (5) A new RPC channel touches packages/shared/src/protocol/channels.ts and the server-core registration; channels are also enumerated by the Electron preload bridge, so check the allowlist there. (6) No persistence boundary: the skip list is derived per run, nothing new is written to disk. (7) Adjacent-but-separate surface not to conflate: the plugin MCP diagnostics path (apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:179-186, :252, :314, :447) already reports plugin-side MCP problems in its own command and must keep doing so unchanged.
userImpact: Concrete and current, though it only bites on the headless surface. A CI job running `nessy-general-agent run --output-format stream-json ... | jq` gets a stream whose first line is already a `text_delta`/`tool_start`; if an enabled MCP source was skipped because its config failed validation (stdio entry with no `command`, HTTP entry with no `url`, or an authenticated source with no token), the run proceeds with that server's tools simply absent and the job sees NO signal — the reason exists only in a `debug()` string that is off unless debug logging is enabled (packages/shared/src/sources/server-builder.ts:110, :127, :164), and the aggregated error list is dropped before anyone can read it (packages/shared/src/mcp/runtime-pool-servers.ts:392 → :428). The observed failure is therefore a silent quality regression: the agent answers without the tool it was supposed to have, and the pipeline exits 0. A terminal (`--output-format text`) run is equally silent — the startup output stops at 'LLM connection configured:' (apps/cli/src/index.ts:759). Second, smaller impact: a consumer written against Claude's stream-json contract crashes or drops the run when its first-line init parse finds no `system`/`init` object.
notes: Every file cited was read this session (apps/cli/src/index.ts, apps/cli/src/plugin.ts, packages/core/src/types/message.ts, packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts, packages/shared/src/sources/server-builder.ts, packages/shared/src/mcp/runtime-pool-servers.ts, packages/shared/src/agent/diagnostics.ts, docs/cli.md) and the doc line was re-fetched with `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog.md` — line 21 matches the quote verbatim. Two things left unverified, neither affecting the verdict: (a) whether the Electron preload bridge maintains an explicit channel allowlist that a new `sessions:*` channel must be added to — named as a check in blastRadius rather than asserted; (b) the exact plumbing depth needed to thread the skip list from `materializeSourceServers` out to a session-scoped read, which is why effort is L rather than M. Design decision embedded above (option (a) in the channels entry — CLI holds the init line until the first snapshot materializes) is mine, not the doc's; the doc only binds the frame's content, not when we compute it. Report ordering note: f133 should be merged with f180 and f125 — one fix (the init frame) closes all three, and effort L is the shared figure, not three times L.
